title: Support ops playbook: task graph interpreter & async task runner
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Our on-call and support teams rely on fragmented bash scripts, ad-hoc Admin CLI commands, and long, free-form runbooks during incidents. This creates variability in execution, poor audit trails, and frequent toil when steps need retries or partial rollbacks.

Goal: Implement a lightweight task graph interpreter and async task runner that treats runbook steps as first-class tasks with retries, idempotency keys, approval gates, and structured audit events. The system should enable:
- Authoring runbooks as ordered DAGs (tasks + conditional transitions) stored in the console.
- A runtime that executes tasks asynchronously with a visibility API for status, logs, and token-level cost estimates.
- Automatic prefix/KV caching integrations for common LLM-powered helper steps.
- Role-based approval gates and integration points for SSO and audit logs (KMS-backed).

Non-goals: Full-on workflow engine with arbitrary scripting, replacing existing long-running orchestration platforms, or supporting every third-party tool out of the gate. Focus is on common support/admin flows (restart service, rotate key, evacuate instance, ingest logs).

Deliverables: runtime library, admin CLI adapters, Console UI hooks for step inspection, audit event schema, integration tests and a demo runbook for incident handling.
acceptance_criteria: Runbooks can be authored as task graphs in Console and saved as JSON/YAML templates.
Runtime executes tasks asynchronously and returns deterministic status transitions (queued -> running -> succeeded/failed -> rollback_if_configured).
Each executed step emits structured audit events containing actor, timestamp, inputs (redacted), idempotency key, and result summary to the central audit log.
Approval gate: steps marked as gated require an explicit CLI or Console approval action before proceeding; approvals are auditable and revocable.
Task retries honor backoff policy and do not duplicate side-effects when idempotency keys are present.
A demo incident runbook shows a 30% reduction in mean time to remediate manual operator steps in internal testing.
Integration tests exercise failure/retry/rollback semantics and validate audit entries are persisted to the compliance sink.
updates: 2025-02-15: Kickoff meeting with SRE, Support, and Console UX. Agreed to prototype interpreter in Go to reuse existing runtime helpers.
2025-02-18: Decided to represent tasks as small, typed actions (shell, http, api-call, lua) rather than freeform scripts to make idempotency feasible.
2025-02-22: Chose event schema for audit logs; working with Security to ensure KMS redaction for secrets in events. Security wants per-step redaction whitelist.
2025-02-25: Implemented basic async queue and worker; validated ordering and backoff with synthetic steps. Identified race when two workers claim same idempotency key — added advisory lock plan.
2025-03-01: UX wireframes for Console task inspector posted. Feedback: expose token cost and KV cache hit rate per step. Filed follow-up for Console hook (ENG-96211).
2025-03-03: Demo to Support team went well; they requested a preflight dry-run mode and a simpler approval UI. Added 'dry_run' to acceptance criteria.
comments: Evan R. (SRE): For restart-service step we need a safe-check to ensure no concurrent canary deployment is running. Add 'precondition' field to tasks.
Priya K. (Security): Audit schema looks good; require encryption-at-rest for stored runbook templates and HSM-backed signing for approvals. Follow-up: security review scheduled.
Asha (Support lead): Demo was promising. Please prioritize the 'dry_run' and 'explain' output for on-call training. We can provide sample runbooks based on recent P0 incidents.
Liam O'Connor (Assignee): Will open draft PR for runtime and CLI adapter by 2025-03-07. Need help from infra on advisory locks (ENG-84109 suggested as reference).
